name: bitcode (compact binary Encode/Decode)
verdict_reason: In the independent 2026-08-07 run, bitcode 0.6.9 serialized 3.98x-6.37x faster and deserialized 1.41x-2.89x faster than bincode 1.3.3 via serde, with the smallest output on log and minecraft_savedata. On float-heavy mesh data it was slower than bincode 2 and about 9x slower to serialize than rkyv, speedy or wincode.
tier_reason: Third-party benchmark with public code; rustc nightly, the CPU and lto = true are stated.
claimed_speedup: vs bincode 1.3.3: serialize 95.792 µs vs 464.75 µs (log), 81.495 µs vs 518.86 µs (minecraft_savedata), 1.2197 ms vs 4.8569 ms (mesh); deserialize 1.1430 ms vs 1.6158 ms, 1.0356 ms vs 1.5229 ms, 1.2589 ms vs 3.6395 ms; size 703710 vs 1045784 bytes (log). vs serde_json (2026-10-05 run): serialize 146.23 µs vs 3.6304 ms, deserialize 1.4627 ms vs 6.1963 ms (log). Ratios 3.98x-6.37x serialize and 1.41x-2.89x deserialize vs bincode (derived from page data)
workload: rust_serialization_benchmark datasets log (many small strings), minecraft_savedata (structured saves) and mesh (float triangles); serialize into a buffer and deserialize into owned Rust types; bitcode uses its own derive, bincode 1.3.3 goes through serde.
hardware: AMD EPYC 9V74 GitHub Actions runner (2026-08-07 run); AMD EPYC 7763 runner (2026-10-05 run)
toolchain: rustc 1.99.0-nightly (2026-08-06) and 1.101.0-nightly (2026-10-04); bench profile lto = true; no target-cpu flag
one_liner: Binary format with its own derive that serializes 4x-6x and deserializes 1.4x-2.9x faster than bincode 1.3 via serde, with smaller output.
how_it_is_fast: Groups all instances of each field together (column-wise, after tree-buf) and stores integers in as few bits as the values need. Code is written so LLVM can auto-vectorize it, and validation runs up front on typed vectors before deserialization.
use_it_when: Rust-to-Rust messages or caches where both serialize speed and size matter
String- and struct-heavy data like the log and minecraft_savedata sets
Data that will be compressed afterwards; the grouped layout compresses well
skip_it_when: Large arrays of plain floats: rkyv, speedy and wincode serialized mesh about 9x faster
You need a format that stays stable across major versions; the README lists that as a non-goal
Other languages must read the data
caveats: bincode was removed from the benchmark in 2026-08 as unmaintained, so the bincode comparison comes from the 2026-08-07 run and the serde_json comparison from the 2026-10-05 run, on different runner CPUs
bitcode's derive is compared with bincode 1.3.3 through serde, so part of the gain is avoiding serde
tradeoffs: Format may change between major versions
Not self-describing; schema lives in the Rust types

evidence.quote: All instances of each field are grouped together making compression easier
